item.statement: The Mo-containing alloy exhibited reduced mechanical performance due to the round morphology of gamma prime particles and the persistence of the needle-like Heusler phase.
item.system: Al 9 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 Mo 1

The worst behavior was exhibited by the Mo-containing alloy
round γ′-particles contributed in a bad way to the mechanical behavior.

item.statement: The Hf-containing alloy suffered from eutectic formation and unsolved Heusler phase during the standard homogenization treatment, requiring a lower temperature adaptation.
item.system: Al 9.5 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 Hf 0.5
quotes: In the case of the Mo-alloy the Heusler type phase was completely dissolved after this treatment, while the Hf-alloy exhibited eutectic formations at the grain boundaries and unsolved Heusler type phase in spherical form
In this case the heat treatment temperature needed to be adapted and finally no eutectic formation occurred at 1140 °C, but the Heusler type phase still remained unsolved
The homogenization treatment for the base alloy (1220 °C/20 h) was supposed to work for Al 9 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 Mo 1 and the Hf-containing alloy as well.

item.statement: While directional solidification significantly improved strength and reduced scatter at lower temperatures, the benefit diminished at high temperatures (800–900 °C).
item.system: Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6
item.lever: processing method (directional solidification vs conventional casting)
quotes: Surprisingly, at higher temperatures of 800 and 900 °C the improvement by DS processing was only small (a factor of 1.1 and 1.0 respectively for 800 and 900 °C).
Differences in UTS of all tested specimen were getting smaller in the higher temperature range 800–900 °C.
On one hand, DS-samples scattered much less, as standard deviation of particularly ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and also strain to failure (ε f ) were reduced strongly for each temperature level

item.statement: Larger gamma prime precipitates achieved by extended annealing at 950 °C led to brittle fracture behavior and high scatter in strain to failure, despite increasing strength at room temperature.
item.system: Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6
quotes: Samples tested at room temperature showed a brittle fracture behavior, as well as specimens tested at 600 and 700 °C.
In general, large scattering occurred respective to strain to failure and curve progression.
Annealing at 900 °C/50 h did in fact lead to smaller precipitates, but these samples exhibited a higher ultimate tensile strength, higher strain to failure and less scatter.
